title: Socratididion’s
html_source:
From ‘The Clouds’ by Aristophanes

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9BMVvIzvEc4

Socrates is mocked in this play, Socratididion is sweet Socrates, Gifford, p207.

anchor.prefix:
earn from Xanthippe? 

1922#182

 — Dialectic, Stephen answered: and from his mother how to bring thoughts into the world. What he learnt from his other wife Myrto (absit nomen!),
anchor.suffix:
Epipsychidion, no man, not a woman, will ever know. But neither the midwife's lore nor the caudlelectures saved him from the archons of Sinn Fein and their naggin of hemlock.
